diagnosis: The image shows that the incumbent is not a jammed optimum at all: only one pair has slack below $10^{-9}$, the next $\sim$600 pairs form a nearly flat plateau within about $1.4\times10^{-6}$ of the maximum, and 97 of 99 points have zero contacts (the remaining two have one each). Consequently a trust-region LP built on the $10^{-9}$-active set is massively underdetermined—it can always push the single tightest pair down until other plateau pairs pop up—while random shakes and smooth repulsion from `best.npy` keep falling back into the same plateau, explaining gains of only $\sim10^{-6}$ over 33 programs. What is missing structurally is a balanced, equioscillating contact network: at a genuine local optimum many pairs should be tied at the maximum, essentially every point should carry several contacts, and per-point maxima should be equalised, pinning the $99\times12$ tangent degrees of freedom. Until such a configuration is reached (in this or a different basin), neither LP polish nor local perturbation can certify or substantially improve the code.
